Sized against the current sale value, the bid has a hard survivable ceiling and the recommended number sits well inside it.

binding_gap: The weakest fielded slot is the attacking one Conté occupies, and the Mokwa trade closes it for a net cash gain rather than a cost. The next-weakest is the fourth defender, whose return is by some distance the lowest in the eleven — but that gap cannot be closed this cycle. The one genuinely large defensive upgrade on the board would need more than twice what a single legal sale can raise, and a two-sale structure would take the squad below eleven. That slot waits for after the lock.

Raise it, then sell Conté the moment it lands. Everything else on the board is an avoid, and the squad is otherwise as good as it can be made before the lock.

sell.reason: Conté only, and strictly after the Mokwa purchase settles — buy first, then sell. He is the lowest-scoring outfielder in the forced eleven and the only sale that keeps the formation legal once an attacker arrives: selling the defender instead would leave a shape the game will not accept. A dated sweep this run has him fit, in his club's projected XI and under a contract extended in the summer; he is sold because he is a rotation player whose per-matchday return is a fraction of the man replacing him.
